prespecification_note: Written and checksum-pinned before the intravenous engine was implemented and before any melphalan curve, Cmax or AUC was computed. Not blinded: the label was read in full, and one hand calculation was made before writing this plan: 100 mg/m2 / 451 ug.min/mL is about 222 mL/min/m2, below the stated 250-325 mL/min/m2. The rules mirror label-exposure-consistency-plan-v1.0 (pomalidomide) with the changes an intravenous drug needs.
not_this: Not validation: a label agreeing with itself says nothing about whether the curve describes patients.
Not an outside-data check; that would be a later step with its own locked plan.
Not a dosing recommendation or an exposure prediction for any patient; melphalan conditioning is given only under specialist care.
question: Can a one-compartment, typical-value intravenous curve built from the EVOMELA label by fixed rules reproduce the label's own statements for patients with multiple myeloma, and which parameter set should the engine use?

inputs.target_population: Multiple myeloma, conditioning before autologous stem cell transplantation
inputs.regimen: 100 mg/m2 as a 30-minute constant-rate intravenous infusion, evaluated as a single infusion. The second infusion 24 h later is not needed for the checks: with a 75-minute half-life less than 0.001% of the first dose remains at 24 h.

model.structure: One compartment, linear, constant-rate infusion, per m2 of body surface area; typical values.
model.concentration: During the infusion (0 <= t <= T): C(t) = R / CL (1 - e^(-k t)), R = dose / T. After it: C(t) = C(T) e^(-k (t - T)). k = CL / V.
model.cmax: C(T), the concentration at the end of the infusion.
model.auc: Dose / CL (AUC from zero to infinity), checked against numerical integration.
model.why_one_compartment: The label gives one half-life and one volume range. Melphalan has a short distribution phase (about 10 minutes in older labels), which a one-compartment curve does not show; the end-of-infusion Cmax check tests how much that matters.

parameter_sets.why_this_order: Set A uses the only quantities the label reports for myeloma patients at the labelled dose (Cmax and AUC0-inf at 100 mg/m2); the clearance and volume ranges do not state their population.

A_exposure_derived_mm.v: CL x t1/2 / ln 2, with t1/2 = 75 minutes.

C2_half_life.compare: ln 2 x V / CL against 75 minutes

C3_cmax_end_of_infusion.compare: Model concentration at the end of the 30-minute infusion against 5.8 ug/mL

C5_volume_in_stated_range.role: descriptive; the type of volume is not stated

checks.which_checks_are_informative: For set A, C1, C2 and C4 hold by construction (its CL comes from the AUC and its V from the half-life), so C3 (end-of-infusion Cmax) is its only informative pass-or-fail check. For set B, all four are informative.

sensitivity.infusion_duration: C3 is also computed for 24- and 48-minute infusions, the range of infusion times reported in the clinical trial (section 6.1: "administered over ~30 minutes (range: 24-48 minutes)"). Reported, not used for selection.

tolerance.rule: A pass-or-fail check passes if model / label is within 0.67 to 1.5 inclusive.
tolerance.why: Same as the pomalidomide plan, so drugs are held to one standard.

decision_rule.selection: The engine uses the first set in order_of_preference that passes C1 to C4 for a 30-minute infusion.
decision_rule.if_none_passes: Melphalan is recorded as not eligible for a label-based curve, with the failing checks.
decision_rule.reporting: Every check for both sets is reported, including for the set not selected.
decision_rule.never: No value is adjusted after seeing results.

scenarios.rule: Each label covariate statement is applied as CL multiplied by its stated factor (ideal body weight 45 kg x 0.72, 100 kg x 1.31; creatinine clearance 30 mL/min x 0.718), one at a time, to the selected set only, with its quote. They are stated for ideal body weight while the curve is per m2; this mismatch is shown with each scenario.
scenarios.not_checked_here: Scenarios are carried into the engine, not tested.
